title: Raise compile and target SDK to the current Play requirement
boundary: **Not in this slice:** upgrading Kotlin, Compose or AGP beyond what the SDK bump forces, and new features.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Google Play only accepts new apps and updates targeting a recent API level. The requirement changes every year, so it must be looked up when releasing.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body: - None. The existing tests and a device walkthrough are the check.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Look up Google Play's current target API requirement in the Play Console help or the Android developer documentation, for new apps and for updates. Record the source and the value with `slicer note S48`. (The earlier note in this roadmap says at least API 35 for new apps since August 2025. Confirm it rather than trusting that.)
2. Set `targetSdk` to that level, and `compileSdk` too if S53 left it lower. Install the matching SDK platform. Update the "Android SDK 34" lines in `DEVELOPERS.md` and `BUILDING.md`.
3. If the new `compileSdk` allows it, `androidx.core:core-ktx` may move to the version in the catalog. Otherwise leave it.
4. Re-test on an emulator at that API level:
   - Edge-to-edge is enforced from API 35: no content may sit under the status or navigation bars, and the Scaffold insets must apply.
   - Notification permission and a delivered reminder.
   - The predictive back gesture from the detail and settings screens (needs S10).
   - Backup export and import.
   - If the target is API 36: predictive back is on by default (check the back animation from every screen, including the Archived screen from S15), and on large screens (sw600dp and up) Android ignores orientation and resizability restrictions, so run the app on a Pixel Tablet emulator in both orientations and in split screen.
5. Fix only what the bump breaks.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest lintDebug assembleDebug assembleRelease` passes.
- The device walkthrough above is done and recorded with `slicer note S48`.
